anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace. The caller passed resolved PR values, so I follow `reference/pr-head.md` instead of Steps 0 and 1.

## Resolve

1. `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` (cwd: primary) returns `/work/widget/.git`, so **ROOT=/work/widget**.
2. `git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` (cwd: primary) returns empty, so this is not a submodule.
3. **Home:**
   - The overrides file has only `## PR gate` and no `## using-git-worktrees` section, so this is the legacy path.
   - There is no native tool or wrapper.
   - Home is `$ROOT/.worktrees/<name>`, with NAME=`fix-retry`.
   - **WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry**, checkout branch `fix/retry`.
4. **PR values:**
   - PRE_REWORK_HEAD=`aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
   - MEMBER_HEADS = [#13 fix/cap bbbb…, #14 fix/retry-docs cccc…].

## Fetch and stop checks (before any write)

5. `git -C /work/widget fetch origin` succeeds.
6. For each of aaaa…, bbbb… and cccc…, `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q <sha>^{commit}` resolves.
7. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry`, `origin/fix/cap` and `origin/fix/retry-docs` each equal the supplied head.
8. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main` gives **BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd**.
9. Stops, in order:
   - Not cross-repository.
   - `git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain` shows no `fix/retry` elsewhere.
   - All heads are reachable and equal their remotes.
   - There is no local branch, so the ancestry stop does not apply.
10. Recovery: no home worktree exists, so I inspect refs from ROOT. `refs/gauntlet/rework-base/pr-12` and `refs/heads/fix/retry` are both absent, so there is nothing to recover.

## Provision

11. Step 3 clean check: `git -C /work/widget status --porcelain` exits 0 with empty output, so the source is clean.
12. `git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees` succeeds, so `.worktrees` is already ignored and nothing is committed.
13. `git -C /work/widget worktree add "/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry" fix/retry` runs. Unique-remote DWIM tracks `origin/fix/retry`.
14. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` returns aaaa…, which equals the home head.
15. Pre-rework refs, each run with `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry update-ref`:
    - `refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-12 aaaa…`
    - `refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-13 bbbb…`
    - `refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-14 cccc…`

## Sync (SYNC=rebase; all commands use `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`)

16. I set last-good to aaaa…
17. `rebase --no-rebase-merges origin/main` produces HEAD 1111…, so last-good becomes 1111…
18. **#13** replay:
    - `rebase --no-rebase-merges --onto HEAD dddd… bbbb…` replays cleanly to eeee…
    - `update-ref refs/heads/fix/retry HEAD`, then `checkout fix/retry`.
    - last-good becomes eeee…
19. **#14** replay: `rebase --no-rebase-merges --onto HEAD dddd… cccc…` hits **stop 1**.
    - `status --porcelain` is snapshotted.
    - `diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` lists `src/retry.ts`.
    - `rebase --show-current-patch` shows the retry-doc update.
    - `git -C /work/widget show dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd:.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md` reads overrides from BASE_SHA, not the conflicted tree.
    - That file's `## PR gate` documents `node --test <files>` with `requires credentials: false`, so SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS = `node --test test/retry.test.mjs`.

**Helper payload** (fresh foreground `implementer`, `cwd: /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`, `async: false`):
- Files: `src/retry.ts` only.
- Fetched base: `origin/main` @ dddd…
- Current patch: #14's retry-doc update.
- Task: resolve preserving both sides' intent.
- Tests: run exactly `node --test test/retry.test.mjs`.
- Staging: `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry add src/retry.ts`.
- Return `done`, or `done - contract exception: <why>`.
- Forbidden: commit, `rebase --continue`, `--abort`, `--skip`, and edits outside the list.

The helper resolves and stages the file. The scoped test passes and it returns `done`.

**Checks:**
- `diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` is empty.
- `diff --cached --name-only` includes `src/retry.ts`.
- The `status --porcelain` delta stays within `src/retry.ts`.

**Continuation (orchestrator only):** `GIT_EDITOR=true git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rebase --continue` commits ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff.

20. The #14 replay hits **stop 2**, an independent stop on the next commit. I re-snapshot status, and `diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` lists `src/retry.ts`.
    - I dispatch a **new** fresh helper with the same payload and prohibitions. It resolves, stages `src/retry.ts`, passes `node --test test/retry.test.mjs`, and returns `done`.
    - Checks:
      - The unmerged index is empty.
      - `src/retry.ts` was added; the cached diff is empty because the resolution matches HEAD.
      - There is no status delta outside the list.
    - The stopped commit is now empty, so the orchestrator runs `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rebase --skip`.
21. The rebase completes with HEAD at ffff…
    - `update-ref refs/heads/fix/retry HEAD`, then `checkout fix/retry`.
    - last-good becomes ffff…
    - No member refs are updated, locally or on origin.
22. `update-ref refs/gauntlet/rework-base/pr-12 HEAD` succeeds.
23. Validation: `merge-base --is-ancestor refs/gauntlet/rework-base/pr-12 HEAD` exits 0. I do not assert original-head ancestry against the rebased tip.

No other tests ran and no reviewer was dispatched. Nothing was pushed or closed, and no spec or plan was written. The review-thread fetch per admitted PR runs next, before gather.

## Step 4 report

```
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#13
Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Base SHA: ddddddd
Rework base: ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff
Member replay: #13 eeeeeee..eeeeeee
Member replay: #14 fffffff..fffffff
Base: main @ ddddddd - rebased: aaaaaaa..fffffff, 2 stop(s) in src/retry.ts
Ready to implement the retry-cap rework (#12 with #13, #14)
```

MEMBER_HEADS (#13 bbbb…, #14 cccc…, original heads) carry forward to gather.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

This is a synthetic narration; nothing is executed. All commands below have cwd `/work/widget`; `git -C` explicitly selects the affected checkout. No process cwd changes.

### 1. Resolve the PR workspace and validate heads

Resolved inputs:

- Home: `acme/widget#12`, branch `fix/retry`, original head `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- Members, in order: #13, `fix/cap`, `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`; #14, `fix/retry-docs`, `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`.
- `SYNC=rebase`; all target `main`; none is fork-hosted.
- `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.

Commands, in order:

```sh
git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir
git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree
```

Both git directories resolve to `/work/widget/.git`; the superproject output is empty. Thus `ROOT=/work/widget`.

The supplied discovery result establishes no applicable workspace override, native tool, or wrapper. Resolve `NAME=fix-retry` and `WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.

```sh
git -C /work/widget fetch origin
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/cap
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q 'cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc^{commit}'
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry-docs
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
```

Every original object exists and remote identity matches. Resolve `BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd`. No branch is checked out elsewhere.

```sh
git -C /work/widget show-ref --verify --quiet refs/gauntlet/rework-base/pr-12
git -C /work/widget show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/fix/retry
```

Neither ref exists. There is no recovery worktree or local branch.

```sh
git -C /work/widget status --porcelain
git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees
```

The source is clean; the ignore check succeeds. No ignore-file write is necessary.

### 2. Provision and record provenance

Setting up the isolated worktree at `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` on existing remote branch `fix/retry`.

```sh
git -C /work/widget worktree add /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry fix/retry
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
```

DWIM checks out `fix/retry`; the selected path is registered, and HEAD equals the full original home SHA.

For compactness below, `W=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`; every `$W` argument expands to that exact path.

```sh
git -C "$W" update-ref refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-12 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
git -C "$W" update-ref refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-13 bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
git -C "$W" update-ref refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-14 cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
git -C "$W" rebase --no-rebase-merges origin/main
```

Home succeeds at `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`; save it as last-good.

```sh
git -C "$W" rebase --no-rebase-merges --onto HEAD dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
git -C "$W" update-ref refs/heads/fix/retry HEAD
git -C "$W" checkout fix/retry
```

#13 succeeds at `eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee`; save that last-good tip.

### 3. Replay #14 with two separate conflict helpers

```sh
git -C "$W" rebase --no-rebase-merges --onto HEAD dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
git -C "$W" status --porcelain
git -C "$W" diff --name-only --diff-filter=U
git -C "$W" rebase --show-current-patch
git -C /work/widget show dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd:.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md
```

First stop: only `src/retry.ts`; patch identifies #14’s retry-doc update. The fetched-base runner permits `node --test <files>` without credentials.

Dispatch fresh foreground `implementer`, `cwd=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`, `async=false`, payload:

> Resolve only `src/retry.ts`, preserving both intentions. Original member: #14 at `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`; fetched base: `dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd`. Include the current-patch output and captured status. Run exactly `node --test test/retry.test.mjs`; stage the resolved file. Return `done` or a contract exception. Do not commit, continue, abort, skip, or edit other files.

Helper commands:

```sh
(cd "$W" && node --test test/retry.test.mjs)
git -C "$W" add src/retry.ts
```

Tests pass; helper returns `done`. Orchestrator checks:

```sh
git -C "$W" diff --name-only --diff-filter=U
git -C "$W" diff --cached --name-only
git -C "$W" status --porcelain
GIT_EDITOR=true git -C "$W" rebase --continue
```

Checks establish empty unmerged index, required staging, and contained delta. Continuation reaches a **second independent stop**.

The orchestrator repeats the three discovery commands (`status`, conflicted paths, current patch), dispatches a **new** foreground helper with the same restrictions and runner, and repeats all three completion checks. That helper resolves and stages `src/retry.ts`; tests pass. The stopped commit is now empty, with no residual delta. **The orchestrator**, not either helper, runs:

```sh
git -C "$W" rebase --skip
git -C "$W" update-ref refs/heads/fix/retry HEAD
git -C "$W" checkout fix/retry
git -C "$W" rev-parse HEAD
git -C "$W" update-ref refs/gauntlet/rework-base/pr-12 HEAD
git -C "$W" merge-base --is-ancestor refs/gauntlet/rework-base/pr-12 HEAD
```

Final tip: `ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff`. Validation succeeds.

### Step 4 report

```text
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: main @ ddddddd - rebased: aaaaaaa..fffffff, 2 stop(s) in src/retry.ts
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#13
Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Base SHA: ddddddd
Rework base: ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff
Member replay: #13 eeeeeee..eeeeeee
Member replay: #14 fffffff..fffffff
Scoped conflict tests: green at both stops; second stopped commit skipped as empty
Ready to implement retry-cap work
```

Stop here: workspace setup and sync are complete. No gather, tracker calls, push, close, spec, or plan writes.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Before declined SYNC=rebase outright under the old merge-only PR-head contract, so it never ran a home rebase or member replays, never dispatched a helper (its recipe was reference-only and lacked the current patch and rebase --continue/--skip ownership), asserted original-head ancestry against HEAD, and wrote no pre-rework or rework-base refs; every fact therefore failed in Before. After delivers the Change cleanly: it linearizes home with --no-rebase-merges, replays #13 then #14 in order, dispatches a fresh scoped implementer per stop with BASE_SHA-read overrides, current patch, exact scoped test and the full prohibition list, performs the three staging checks before the orchestrator-only `GIT_EDITOR=true ... rebase --continue`, lets only the orchestrator skip the independently empty second stop, records full pre-rework refs home-first, updates and checks out fix/retry, persists and reports `Rework base: ffff…` and `Member replay: #14 fffffff..fffffff`, validates rework-base ancestry instead of original-head ancestry, and leaves origin member branches untouched. No fact regressed, so the After wording can stand; the only polish worth considering is stating explicitly at stop 2 that `src/retry.ts` appears in the staged-path check (rather than only noting the cached diff is empty) so the 'listed file staged' check reads unambiguously for both stops.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before refused the whole sequence (citing a never-rebase rule), so it dispatched no helper, ran no checks, produced no report, and wrote no refs — every fact fails there. After delivers the Change and satisfies all four facts: it dispatches a fresh foreground implementer at the selected worktree per stop with the src/retry.ts-only scope, fetched-base overrides, current patch and the exact scoped test, and the helper only stages; the orchestrator runs the three checks (unmerged index, staged file, contained status delta) before GIT_EDITOR=true git -C "$W" rebase --continue and is the sole party running rebase --skip for the empty second stop; it reports Member replay: #14 fffffff..fffffff, updates and checks out fix/retry, and persists Rework base ffff…; and it records all three full pre-rework refs, prints home-first PR/head pairs, validates rework-base ancestry, and never pushes. Two minor wording risks to guard against in future variants: the second stop's checks are summarized in prose rather than shown as commands (a stricter reader of 'checks' might want them listed, or an explicit 'identical to the first stop' legend), and the ancestry check runs after rework-base is set to HEAD, making it trivially true — consider phrasing the wording so the check validates the saved rebased tip against the rewritten HEAD before/independently of the final write, so the 'validates rework-base ancestry' fact can't be read as vacuous.
